account: It is just after ten on day 0, and I have arrived at the plaza for my scheduled market walk. I have not yet seen or heard evidence of any secret activity. My feeling that something is happening without me remains a suspicion, not a finding. The one unresolved detail is today's three o'clock tea: the appointment book says only 'the neighbour, dockside cottage (east bank),' without a name or cottage number. The secretary says no correspondence or news has reached her and has agreed to investigate the invitation at the docks before tea. She now has the appointment book safely with her. I can see her walking nearby, three townsfolk gathered close to me, and the person known as neighbour walking farther away. I have not heard their conversations or learned why they are here. The tea could simply be an ordinary social appointment with incomplete directions; I have no basis yet to attach another purpose to it. I intend to keep my public appointments and learn what residents have actually seen or heard.
